queue.detail: TARGET: F173 (A) by default -- runner management is free-typed text that swallows its own refusal, while openspec/specs/runner-registry/spec.md:72-73 is a SHIPPED requirement saying it must offer the catalog's models. The design surface is larger than the model field: hub/ui/src/api/runners.ts:69-88 declare onSuccess and NO onError, hub/ui/src/main.tsx:8-15 configures no MutationCache onError and no toast, and RunnersPage.tsx renders exactly one error surface (deleteError). So a refused create or edit reaches nothing, and that absence is systemic rather than local to runners -- decide deliberately how wide the change is, and say so in design.md. OVERRIDE RULE: if D-1 filed a NEW A-severity finding, spec that instead; the playbook ranks this window's own drive above the ledger. Either way RECORD THE CHOSEN TARGET IN THE LOG -- R2 and R3 need a target that does not move under them. Write proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md and the specs/<capability>/spec.md deltas into openspec/changes/<name>/. `openspec new change` refuses a name starting with a digit. SHALL must be on a requirement's FIRST physical line -- --strict reads only that line. `openspec validate --strict <name>` must pass before the round is done. Specs live in openspec, NEVER also in the Hub.

decisions_for_user.question: Ratify or widen the fastmcp <4 ceiling taken unattended at 01:27 (4ce24fc).
decisions_for_user.evidence: DEPBENCH (arXiv 2608.30300, 2026-08-31) measures the best coding-agent configuration repairing 104/203 = 51.2% of real dependency upgrades containing hidden code-level changes. A fastmcp break means every agent turn fails to START, not a red test, so a coin flip is not a migration strategy. The bound plus hub/tests/test_fastmcp_api_contract.py is the defensible posture. The same paper argues AGAINST reflexively extending the pattern to fastapi>=0.110, where a break is a failing test -- the case agents handle best.
